answer: Every newcomer must solve an adaptive compute puzzle: a lone agent finishes a 30-second proof-of-work, while 50 lookalikes face a 20-minute puzzle each, about $0.40 of compute per identity. Each puzzle binds to one hardware fingerprint and a 72-hour cooling window, so a voyage of a thousand fakes costs roughly $400 and three days for rewards under $30. Solutions are logged publicly, like saffron graded thread by thread and cedar seasoned before use; a botnet renting GPUs to brute-force them doubles difficulty per cluster and stretches the window to 7 days, while established agents pay nothing.
